conviction_note: Six findings sum naively to about -10.5 but three of them share one root (a shrinking revenue base that no filing-driven feed can see), so I discount to -6.0, which is roughly a 1-sigma day on 87% realised vol and sits inside the -8.05%/-5.99% range of the only two clean prints this company has ever had; the +11.95% five-day run-up in the baseline is a buyback-headline echo that is already fading, not earnings anticipation.

findings.finding: The Q4 FY2026 revenue guide of US$23-26m given on 2026-06-08 implies a year-over-year decline of -15.0% to -24.8%, two to three times the -7.5%/-7.8%/-9.1% printed in Q1/Q2/Q3, because Q4 FY2025 revenue was US$30.6m -- a figure the company has never reported and that only exists as FY2025 US$118.0m minus nine-month FY2025 US$87,390,942.
findings.why_not_priced: The deceleration is invisible without a two-document subtraction. Gamehaus reports six-month and nine-month cumulative figures, so Q4 FY2025 was never disclosed as a standalone quarter and appears in no data vendor's quarterly series. There are no sell-side EPS estimates and no options chain, so no mechanism exists that would have published or embedded this arithmetic. If the market had done it, the June 8 release would not have been covered on the wires as a guidance beat with 'net income up 16.4%' and the stock would not have needed the Aug 31 buyback pop to be up 11.95% into the print.
findings.independence: The FY2025 total of US$118.0m that completes the subtraction is in a different SEC-filed exhibit, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2000530/000149315225012895/ex99-1.htm (2025-09-09), and the Q4 FY2026 guide itself is in a third document, https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/06/08/tmt-newswire/pr-newswire/gamehaus-holdings-inc-announces-unaudited-financial-results-for-the-third-quarter-of-fiscal-2026-ended-march-31-2026/2360579 (URL path /2026/06/08/ confirms the year). Directionally corroborated from a wholly separate source by finding 4 (the promised RPG launches that were supposed to reverse the decline are not visible).

findings.finding: On 2026-08-12 the company said it will 'progressively optimize its third-party publishing business in casual titles, and in particular in the social casino category' and is now running its existing portfolio 'with user acquisition and operating expenditure allocated according to return on investment rather than scale' effective the current quarter -- and that release traded 22,679 shares, under 6% of the baseline's 408,260 twenty-day average, closing $0.79 to $0.74 to $0.70.
findings.why_not_priced: Gamehaus has guided next-quarter revenue in every single release (Q3 guide US$24-26m, Q4 guide US$23-26m), so the September 8 release carries the first forward guide computed under harvest economics on the business that produces ~90% of revenue via in-app purchases. Twenty-three thousand shares is roughly $17,000 of notional -- the strategy change was not traded, it was ignored. The release was also never furnished on Form 6-K (see finding 6), so it is absent from every filings-driven feed. If this were priced, the 22,679-share session would instead look like the 7.3m-share session nine trading days later.
findings.independence: Volume and closes independently confirmed by https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/GMHS/chart/ (22,679 shares, $0.74 on 08/12/2026) and by https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/gmhs/history/ (22,908 shares). Separately, https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/GMHS-Q/pressreleases/2380124/gamehaus-q3-earnings-call-highlights/ (2026-06-08) has management already describing the UA pullback as 'a direct result' of a decision to 'focus on higher-value players', which is the same policy nine weeks earlier and confirms the direction of travel.

findings.finding: The baseline's +11.95% five-day run-up is almost entirely one session -- 2026-08-31, 7,314,944 shares (about 27% of the 27,038,542 non-affiliate shares the F-3 counts) and +16.51% to $0.85 -- reacting to a 6-K filed 2026-08-28 that merely extended a US$5m buyback of which only ~US$600,000 (518,063 shares) had been used in twelve months; the identical event a year earlier produced +103.54% on ~46m shares and fully retraced.
findings.why_not_priced: The baseline hands the run-up forward as if it were positioning into the print. It is not: the 6-K contains no new authorisation, no new dollars and an admission that 88% of the existing $5m went unused, and the pop is already unwinding ($0.85, $0.84, $0.82, $0.79, $0.82 across Aug 31 to Sep 4). A run-up that actually reflected earnings anticipation would not be a single 350x-normal-volume day on a document with no new economics in it, and would not have started decaying within one session.
findings.independence: The 2025 precedent is a separate document pair: the original authorisation 6-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2000530/000149315225012459/form6-k.htm (2025-08-29) and the reaction reported at https://www.tipranks.com/news/why-is-gamehaus-stock-gmhs-up-105-today (dated 2025-08-30 in the document itself -- note this article is served by search engines as current-year copy and is NOT a 2026 story). The baseline's own avg_volume_20d of 408,260 against a normal 5,000-70,000 daily range is third-party arithmetic confirming one enormous session dominates the window.

findings.finding: The FY2027 growth premise management gave on 2026-06-08 -- 'the user base to return to growth as multiple new titles launch through fiscal 2027', with one RPG live by end of Q2 calendar 2026, one 'launching around September' and one signed for an August-to-September launch -- has no visible trace: neither Apple developer account (GAMEHAUS PTE. LTD, 5 apps; GAMEHAUS LIMITED, 4 apps) lists a single RPG title, and the Aug 12 strategy release does not mention the RPG pipeline at all.
findings.why_not_priced: MAU fell to 3,107k from 3,782k and DAU to 506k from 674k, and the entire case for that reversing was three named-by-genre RPG launches on dated timelines. Two of those three windows have now closed. Nobody reconciles a June call commitment against a September app-store shelf on a $46m uncovered name -- there is no analyst to ask the question on the call, and the Aug 12 release quietly substituted an AI-tools narrative for the RPG narrative without acknowledging the swap. If the launches had happened the company would have issued launch PRs, as it does for everything else.
findings.independence: Two separate Apple developer pages read directly: https://apps.apple.com/us/developer/gamehaus-pte-ltd/id1664707862 and https://apps.apple.com/us/developer/gamehaus-limited/id1562307552 (both read 2026-09-07), showing only casino, bingo, merge, tile-match and interactive-story titles. Caveat stated honestly: mobile publishers do soft-launch under separate accounts and in non-US geos, so this is suggestive rather than conclusive.

findings.finding: A dilution and entrenchment sequence executed in five weeks and never described anywhere as a sequence: Class B voting power raised from 15 to 50 votes per share by shareholder vote on 2026-07-10 (15,598,113 Class B shares, so ~95% of votes), a US$200,000,000 primary Form F-3 shelf filed 2026-07-28 stating a non-affiliate float of US$23,523,531.54, that shelf going EFFECT 2026-08-11/12 -- the same window as the AI narrative release -- and no 424B on file as of 2026-09-07, meaning the ~US$7.8m baby-shelf capacity (one third of float) is entirely unused and live.
findings.why_not_priced: A $200m registration on a $23.5m float is arithmetically absurd unless it is scaffolding, and the useful number -- one third of float, about $7.8m, or 33% of the tradable float at $0.815 -- appears in no wire story and cannot appear in an options skew because there is no options market. The super-voting bump immediately preceding the shelf removes the only constraint on issuing Class A freely, and control was never actually at risk at 15x, so the bump only makes sense ahead of large Class A issuance. If this were priced, the Aug 11/12 EFFECT would have shown up as volume; it showed up as 19,273 then 22,679 shares.
findings.independence: Separate documents: the voting change is in the 6-K at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2000530/000149315226033100/form6-k.htm (2026-07-14, vote held 2026-07-10), and the absence of any 424B plus the EFFECT date are read off https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0002000530.json (read 2026-09-07). The July 10 Nasdaq minimum-bid deficiency letter, deadline 2027-01-06, at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2000530/000149315226032918/ex99-1.htm points the same way, since a sub-$1.00 issuer needing a cure by January has a reason to act on both the shelf and a reverse split.

findings.finding: Seven Section 16 initial statements (Form 3) were filed for Gamehaus insiders with event date 2026-03-18, including founder-level CTO/director/10% owner Yan Xi reporting 5,314,953 Class A shares through Joystick Holding Limited -- people who have been insiders since the January 2025 listing -- even though foreign private issuers are exempt from Section 16 and the company continued to file 6-Ks and a Form F-3 afterwards.
findings.why_not_priced: I cannot explain it and I am reporting it as unexplained rather than asserting a cause. Initial Form 3s filed en bloc by long-standing insiders is the signature of an issuer that has ceased to qualify as a foreign private issuer, which would put the FY2026 annual report on Form 10-K with per-officer compensation and US-GAAP quarterly detail instead of a 20-F -- but the July 2026 F-3 is an FPI-only form, which contradicts that. Either reading is a disclosure-quality datapoint. Nobody screens Form 3 filings by an FPI because they are not supposed to exist, so no coverage or price signature would show whether the market noticed.
findings.independence: A second Form 3 from the same cluster, filed a fortnight later for director Zhu Lei with the identical 2026-03-18 event date and zero holdings: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2000530/000149315226015026/xslF345X06/ownership.xml (filed 2026-04-03). No company statement explaining the change was found in any 6-K.

findings.finding: Neither of the two most material press releases of 2026 was ever furnished on Form 6-K: EDGAR full-text search returns zero hits for 'Third Quarter of Fiscal 2026' under CIK 0002000530 while the same search for 'Second Quarter of Fiscal 2026' returns two, so the last EDGAR-visible revenue datapoint for GMHS is US$26.3m for the December 2025 quarter and the June 8 Q3 release and August 12 strategy change exist only on the wires.
findings.why_not_priced: Sized at zero deliberately: this is the transmission mechanism for findings 1, 2 and 4 rather than an independent move driver, and I am declaring it as such so it is not counted twice. It is the concrete answer to why a nine-month revenue trajectory and a strategy change on the 90%-of-revenue business can sit unpriced in a listed equity -- every screener, XBRL feed and quant pipeline that reads filings has GMHS stale at 2025-12-31, and the only two systems that could have corrected that (sell-side estimates and an options chain) do not exist for this name.
findings.independence: Control query proving the search works and that the gap is real, not a search artefact: https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22Second+Quarter+of+Fiscal+2026%22&ciks=0002000530 returns 2 hits, both accession 0001493152-26-012057 filed 2026-03-23. Corroborated structurally by the full filing index at https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0002000530.json, which shows no 6-K between 2026-03-23 and 2026-06-24 and none in August before the 08-28 buyback filing. Shares document set with finding 2.

searched_and_found_nothing: Title-level app-store rank and gross-revenue trend for the April-June 2026 quarter -- the flagship social casino title is identified on the June 8 call only as 'GCS', which maps to no App Store or Google Play listing I could find, and no free source gave me dated download or revenue-rank series for the nine identifiable Gamehaus apps

App-store review volume and rating trend as a proxy for Q4 engagement -- Apple pages returned ratings totals (Double Win Slots 4.9 / 440K) but no dated review-count series and ambiguous 'last updated' years, so nothing datable enough to rest a finding on

The identity, size, counterparty and any related-party status of the 'minority equity investment in a promising early-stage studio focused on AI-driven game generation' completed 'earlier in 2026' -- disclosed for the first time in the Aug 12 wire release, named in no 6-K, no amount given; this is a genuine unknown the FY2026 balance sheet will resolve and I could not size it

Any explanation for the 2026-08-31 session other than the buyback extension -- no 424B, no 6-K, no 13D/G, no halt and no news item that day; 7.31m shares on nothing is consistent with the buyback echo but I could not exclude an unregistered block or promotional activity
Whether a reverse split is being prepared to cure the minimum bid price by 2027-01-06 -- the July 13 press release explicitly does not mention one, and no proxy or 6-K proposing one has been filed

The reaction to the 2026-06-08 Q3 print as a usable base rate -- it is unusable, because that session was the collapse of a pre-existing momentum squeeze (pre-market above $1.80, close near $1.04) and I could not obtain a clean prior close from any free source; I did not substitute it

Google Play developer listings for Gamehaus (the com.gamehaus.* package guesses 404) and the company's own website, which returned no game list or changelog through this tooling; ir.gamehaus.com was already 403 to the sweep

Supplier and customer read-throughs -- the 20-F names AppLovin and Sinointeractive as significant suppliers (20.5% and 15.1% of accounts payable at FY2025) but neither has said anything about Gamehaus specifically since it last spoke
baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with because there is no options market, but everything I found cuts hard against the baseline's +11.95% five-day run-up -- that run-up is one 7.3m-share session reacting to a buyback extension with no new dollars in it, an event whose 2025 twin produced +103.5% and fully retraced, so the baseline's single directional-looking input is the thing I am most confident is wrong.
